pr_title: Fix IsPrefix and IsSuffix with ignored characters
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/67313

While performing string `StartsWith` or `EndsWith` operations we try to optimize when having ASCII characters. We apply the optimization only if we don't have characters outside ASCII range nor we don't have characters need special handling (like `\0` which treated as ignored character). We detect the special character by using the internal table `HighCharTable`.  In some cases, we can have the source string be shorter than string we check (e.g. doing something like `"A".StartsWith("A\0")` , we check the remaining character `\0` if it is ASCII but we don't check if it is special character using `HighCharTable`. This cause StartsWith/EndsWith return the wrong result. 
The fix is simply adding the check using `HighCharTable` to ensure the correct result.

issue_context.title: string.StartsWith() displays unexpected behaviour on Unix?
issue_context.body:
Through an exception in our software I recently got to learn about certain behaviours of string.StartsWith() depending on culture and even operating system. 
Who would have thought that a shorter string can actually start with a longer string 😕 `"A".StartsWith("Aــــــــــ")`.

Now to the question:
Is `"A".StartsWith("A\0")` returning false on Unix expected behaviour?

Opposed to that `"A\0A".EndsWith("AA")`, `"A\0".EndsWith("A")` and `"A".StartsWith("\0A")` all return true on Unix.

> Is "A".StartsWith("A\0") returning false on Unix expected behaviour?

No. This is a bug.
@tarekgh  Are these behaviors defined? Where can I find the document?

@skyoxZ If you are performing linguistic operations (I mean you are not passing StringComparison.Ordina[IgnoreCase], then the behavior will depend on the [UNICODE COLLATION ALGORITHM](https://unicode.org/reports/tr10/). It will be impossible to document all possible cases for all languages. You may look at [ICU Collation](https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/) doc.

For the specific case mentioned in this issue using the character `\0`. This character is defined as an ignored character for the collation (like if it doesn't exist in the string). You may look at the [Unicode Ignored Characters](https://www.unicode.org/charts/collation/chart_Ignored.html) to see the whole list of the ignored characters.
